labs/pg-firstscene.title: A circle’s first journey
labs/pg-firstscene.description: A small scene has a complete beginning and end: reveal a circle, move it across the frame, hold, then fade it away.
walkthrough: The circle is positioned before it is added. `Create` reveals that existing geometry rather than constructing another object.
The awaited `Scene.play` calls form a sequence. The movement uses `Rate.easeInOutCubic`, so the circle eases into and out of its travel before the final `FadeOut`.
experiments: Change the movement duration from 1600 to 800 and compare the pace.
Replace the easing with `Rate.linear()` and look at the beginning and end of the move.

labs/pg-sequencescene.title: Together, then one at a time
labs/pg-sequencescene.description: The two shapes are revealed together, then take turns moving toward the center. This makes scheduling visible.
walkthrough: `Concurrent` gives the two creation animations one shared starting point. Both can finish before the next awaited play call begins.
`Sequential` runs the circle’s `CustomAnimation` before the rectangle’s. Each callback assigns a position from normalized progress rather than adding an offset every frame.
experiments: Swap the two animations inside `Sequential` and predict which shape moves first.
Replace `Sequential` with `Concurrent` and compare their arrival times.

labs/pg-hierarchyscene.title: Rotate a family of shapes
labs/pg-hierarchyscene.description: A circle and rectangle stay opposite one another while their parent turns through a quarter rotation.
walkthrough: The plain `Entity` is a structural parent. `Entity.add` attaches both children, and the scene then adds that parent.
Animating the parent transforms the entire subtree. The children keep their own local positions, so the shared rotation changes their world positions.
experiments: Change the angle from `Math.PI / 2` to `Math.PI` and watch both children orbit.
Move one child farther from the parent before playback and compare its longer path.

labs/pg-layoutscene.title: Let the bounds do the placing
labs/pg-layoutscene.description: A title, circle and rectangle form a vertical stack without hand-written positions for each object.
walkthrough: `VBox.arrange` measures the supplied entities and uses a gap to place them around a chosen center. It leaves them independently owned by the scene.
`Camera.frame` fits the combined bounds. The three awaited animations then reveal the items in reading order.
experiments: Increase the gap from 0.5 to 1 and observe how the camera fit responds.
Make the rectangle wider and compare the stack’s alignment and framing.

labs/pg-pathscene.title: One path, two bends
labs/pg-pathscene.description: A quadratic path first bends upward, then replaces its geometry with a downward bend.
walkthrough: The SVG-style path string contains a move and a quadratic segment. An analytical path renderer draws its outline with no fill.

After `Create` finishes and the scene waits, `Path.setVertices` replaces the path data. `Scene.invalidate` requests the redraw. This is a geometry change, rather than an animation between the two curves.
experiments: Change the control point from 4 to 1 and compare how far the curve bows.
Give the path a fill and inspect the region implied by its open contour.

labs/pg-booleanscene.title: Make the overlap into geometry
labs/pg-booleanscene.description: Two translucent circles reveal a green intersection that can be styled as its own shape.
walkthrough: The input circles overlap because their centers are closer than two radii. `Intersection` computes the region they share.
The result receives its own fill, stroke and z-index, then fades into view. Its appearance is independent of the translucent input styling.
experiments: Move the circles farther apart and inspect the smaller intersection.
Try `Union` or `Difference` in place of `Intersection` and predict the region before running it.

labs/pg-modifierscene.title: Reveal a path through a modifier
labs/pg-modifierscene.description: The visible portion of a curve grows as the trim endpoint advances.
walkthrough: `TrimModifier` is attached when the path is constructed. Its start remains zero while its end initially exposes only one tenth of the path.
`CustomAnimation` maps progress to `trim.end`, ending at one. The modifier changes which portion is emitted without replacing the original path string.
experiments: Hold the start at 0.25 and watch the reveal begin farther along the path.
Animate start and end together to make a short segment travel along the curve.

labs/pg-sketchscene.title: A reproducible hand-drawn card
labs/pg-sketchscene.description: A rectangle becomes a rough outlined card with hatching inside it.
walkthrough: `VectorEntity.toExcalidraw` applies the clean preset with explicit stroke and fill settings. The seed makes the procedural strokes repeatable.
The scene adds the styled entity and reveals it with `Create`. The original rectangle dimensions still provide its placement and framing.
experiments: Change seed 42 and compare the different stroke irregularities.
Change fillStyle from hachure to another supported style and inspect the interior.

labs/pg-formulascene.title: Write a mathematical expression
labs/pg-formulascene.description: Euler’s identity becomes scene geometry that can be framed and revealed like other entities.
walkthrough: `Tex` receives the LaTeX string and typography options. `Camera.frame` uses its resulting bounds to choose a comfortable view.
`Write` reveals the expression across its constituent geometry. The final wait leaves time to read it.
experiments: Replace the expression with a fraction or summation and compare the new bounds.
Increase the writing duration and pause to inspect the order of the reveal.

labs/pg-maskscene.title: Move the picture inside the letters
labs/pg-maskscene.description: A generated striped image rotates behind a fixed GPU text-shaped mask.
walkthrough: The helper canvas supplies a bitmap without a network image. `Sprite` gives that bitmap a size in the scene.
`Mask` combines the text boundary and the sprite. The animation rotates only the content, so the letters stay in place while the visible stripes move inside them.
experiments: Replace GPU with another short label and observe the new boundary.
Change the stripe count while preserving the same mask to separate image detail from mask geometry.

labs/pg-modelscene.title: Watch a box turn in perspective
labs/pg-modelscene.description: The box’s orientation changes while the camera stays at an oblique angle.
walkthrough: `Box` supplies the mesh and material settings. The camera switches to perspective, sets a 45-degree field of view in radians, and looks at the box.
The animator makes a full Y-axis turn with linear easing. A fixed camera makes the changing faces and shading easy to compare.
experiments: Use orthographic projection to compare how depth affects the silhouette.
Change roughness and inspect the faces as the object rotates.

labs/pg-camerascene.title: Move the observer, keep the subject
labs/pg-camerascene.description: A camera movement changes the view of a stationary box.
walkthrough: The scene places the camera above and to one side of the subject, then uses `Camera.lookAt` to establish the starting view.
`CameraMove` animates the camera position over 2500 milliseconds. The box remains the same entity throughout the movement.
experiments: Choose a farther destination and compare the apparent size at the end.
Change the camera field of view before playback and compare the same movement.

labs/pg-orbitscene.title: Orbit around a visible center
labs/pg-orbitscene.description: The amber dot marks the center while a cyan circle makes one complete orbit around it.
walkthrough: The actor begins three scene units away from the center. `OrbitAnimation` receives both entities, so the center supplies the orbital reference.
The angle is a full turn in radians, and linear easing keeps progress evenly distributed through the 3500-millisecond duration.
experiments: Move the actor farther from the center and compare its path radius.
Use a half turn or a different rate function to change the journey.

labs/pg-interactionscene.title: A shape responds to the pointer
labs/pg-interactionscene.description: Drag the dot, hover over it, then click it to compare three kinds of input-driven change.
walkthrough: `Entity.setDraggable` lets the interaction system move the dot. Separate pointer-over and pointer-out handlers switch its fill color.
The click handler multiplies the current scale by 1.08. Repeated clicks therefore keep growing the dot, unlike a slider that assigns an absolute scale.
experiments: Click several times and compare the cumulative growth.
Replace the click’s `scale` with `setScale` to make repeated clicks select one fixed size.

labs/pg-updatescene.title: An updater draws a continuous path
labs/pg-updatescene.description: The dot follows an ellipse computed from scene time.
walkthrough: `Scene.always` runs the callback as time advances. The conversion from milliseconds to seconds makes the trigonometric expression easier to reason about.
Every update assigns coordinates from cosine and sine. The X amplitude is three and the Y amplitude is two, so the path is an ellipse rather than a circle.
experiments: Make both amplitudes equal and watch the path become circular.
Multiply seconds by two to double the angular speed without changing the path.

labs/pg-trackerscene.title: Animate the input, redraw the result
labs/pg-trackerscene.description: A sine wave gains more oscillations as its frequency tracker changes from one to three.
walkthrough: The graph function reads `ValueTracker.value` whenever it is sampled. Animating the tracker changes the mathematical input rather than animating individual vertices.
The update-phase callback calls `FunctionGraph2D.updateGraph`, so the geometry is regenerated from the current frequency as the animation progresses.
experiments: Change the tracker destination to 0.5 and compare the longer wavelength.
Remove the graph updater, rerun, and notice that changing a value alone does not resample the existing path.

labs/pg-plotscene.title: Data coordinates meet scene coordinates
labs/pg-plotscene.description: A sine graph and a highlighted point share the same axes.
walkthrough: `Axes` defines numeric ranges and a physical width and height. The axes convert mathematical coordinates into scene positions.
`FunctionGraph2D` samples sine against those axes, while `Axes.getDot` places a marker at the corresponding mathematical point. `Create` then reveals the graph.
experiments: Change xRange while keeping width fixed and compare the horizontal scale.
Move the dot to another sine coordinate and check that it stays on the curve.

labs/pg-sdfscene.title: Cut a volume with a distance field
labs/pg-sdfscene.description: A box-shaped subtraction carves into a sphere, and a rotating view reveals the resulting volume.
walkthrough: `SDFSphere.subtract` combines two signed distance fields. This describes the boundary mathematically rather than building a boolean triangle mesh.
`SDFEntity3D` renders the combined field. A perspective camera and a half-turn animation reveal the cut from several angles.
experiments: Change the box dimensions and compare the opening.
Replace subtract with union or intersection to explore different field combinations.

labs/pg-morphscene.title: Turn one silhouette into another
labs/pg-morphscene.description: A cyan circle changes into an amber square over one eased transition.
walkthrough: Only the circle is added initially. `Morph` receives the source and the target entity, using both to define the geometric and styling transition.
The cubic easing changes how quickly the shape travels through the intermediate states. The final hold makes the target shape easy to compare with the starting circle.
experiments: Use a triangle or another path as the target and inspect the intermediate contour.
Slow the duration and pause halfway to see how point correspondence affects the transition.

labs/pg-instancedscene.title: Many shapes share one template
labs/pg-instancedscene.description: An eight-by-eight field of alternating circles rotates as one instanced entity.
walkthrough: `Instanced` uses a circle as its geometry template. Per-instance positions and colors supply the differences between the 64 copies.
`updateInstances` commits those values before the field is added. Animating the field’s transform then moves every instance together without creating 64 scene entities.
experiments: Change the per-instance colors while keeping the template unchanged.
Increase the instance count and adjust the grid loops together; inspect how the shared geometry scales to a larger field.
